# **<u>ORDER</u>** 

The present Petition has been filed by the Petitioner, JSW Hydro Energy Limited, 

seeking the following reliefs: 

_“a) Relax the obligation to declare proportionate overload capacity to the longterm beneficiaries of KWHEP for the period from 15.05.2026 to 15.09.2026, and permit the Petitioner to declare and supply the 10% overload capacity in its entirety, exclusively to the Government of Himachal Pradesh or its nominee; and/or_ 

_b) pass such further order or orders as this Hon’ble Commission may deem fit and proper in the circumstances of the case.”_ 

Order in Petition No. 427/MP/2026 

Page 2 

2. The present Petition was filed on 7.5.2026, and the matter was listed for hearing on 18.9.2026. During the hearing on 18.9.2026,  learned counsel for the Petitioner submitted that the period for which relief was sought in this Petition, i.e., the rainy season from 15.5.2026 to 15.09.2026, had expired, and as such, he prayed that the Petitioner be granted time to either file an amendment application or an application to withdraw the matter, with liberty to file a fresh Petition on the subject matter for the subsequent period.  Learned counsel for the Respondent, HPPC, also pointed out that the period for which the reliefs are sought had already expired.  Accordingly, the matter was adjourned. 

<mark>3. Thereafter, the matter was taken up for hearing on 6.11.2026, when the learned counsel for the Petitioner sought permission to withdraw the Petition with liberty to file a fresh Petition on the subject matter for the subsequent period, as the period for which the reliefs sought had already expired and, as such, this Petition had become infructuous. The learned counsel further submitted that, in this regard, the Petitioner has also filed an affidavit dated 23.10.2026.</mark> 

4. We have considered the parties’ submissions and perused the Petitioner’s affidavit dated 23.10.2026. Considering the Petitioner’s submissions in its affidavit dated 23.10.2026, we allow the Petitioner to withdraw this Petition with liberty to file a fresh Petition on the subject matter for a subsequent period, which will be dealt with in accordance with law. 

5. Accordingly, Petition No. 427/MP/2026 is disposed of, as withdrawn.

**20.** The rationale of the Scheme, as submitted by the Petitioners, is to consolidate the business for the creation of a single larger unified entity and reduce the number of entities within the group to achieve operational and management efficiencies, simplification of administrative tasks, and a simplified organisational structure. It has also been submitted that the amalgamation, pursuant to the Scheme, would inter alia, have the advantages of (i) consolidation of business, which would achieve simplification of administrative tasks, improve management efficiencies, streamline the decision making process, and at the same time maintaining the Powergrid Corporation of India Ltd’s Tariff based competitive bidding based business u/s 63 of the Act distinct from its Regulated tariff mechanism business u/s 62 of the Act; and (ii) reduction in the number of companies within the group as well as achieving reduction multiplicity of legal and regulatory compliances. It is noted that the proposed consolidation is for the ease of business operation, without affecting the tariff, nature, and operation of the transmission assets, and without affecting the interests of the stakeholders. We find that the Petitioners have complied with the requirements stipulated under the Act and TSA regarding amalgamation or merger of Petitioner No. 1 to Petitioner No. 11 with Petitioner No. 12 pursuant to the Scheme of Arrangement under Sections 230-233 of the Companies Act, 2013.
